Where it began

Mitchell Santner was born in Hamilton, in the Waikato, on 5 February 1992, and went to Hamilton Boys' High School. He made his way in the game with Northern Districts, and a strong 2014-15 domestic season pushed him towards the national side.

When Daniel Vettori retired after the 2015 World Cup, New Zealand went looking for a new left-arm spinner. Santner was the answer. Called into the touring party for England that summer, he made 94 in a warm-up game against Somerset and soon had his first one-day cap, at Edgbaston.

The player

His Test debut, against Australia in November 2015, made a little history: it was a day/night match, and nobody before him had begun a Test career under lights. He hit the very first ball he faced for four.

In November 2019 he made his first Test hundred against England at Bay Oval, sharing a stand of 261 with BJ Watling, a New Zealand record for the seventh wicket. His finest hour with the ball came at Pune in October 2024, where he took 7 for 53 and 6 for 104 as New Zealand claimed their first ever Test series win on Indian soil. By November 2026 he had played 33 Tests, taking 80 wickets at 33.95 and scoring 1,089 runs with a best of 126. He had also led New Zealand in two Tests and won both.

What made him special

Santner bowls slow left-arm spin, and he spent a long time working on a carrom ball in private before he trusted it in international cricket. With the bat he is a left-hander who can put on a stand with anyone, as Watling would tell you, and he once took 28 off an over from Adil Rashid in a one-day game.

Home conditions have not always been his friend. In New Zealand the seamers usually get first go, and when he took three wickets against England in 2019, he ended a run of 101 Test wickets in a row on home soil that had all gone to the quick bowlers. A spinner in New Zealand learns to be patient.

Away from the middle

In December 2024 Santner took over from Kane Williamson as New Zealand's white-ball captain. He led them to the final of the 2025 Champions Trophy, having been part of the side that reached the 2019 World Cup final. He won the IPL with Chennai Super Kings in 2023 before joining Mumbai Indians, and he plays the odd round of golf when the cricket allows.

And finally

For Chennai once, with the last ball of a match against Rajasthan Royals, he hit a six to win it. For a man best known for his quiet spin, he has a lovely sense of timing.
